newsitem.title: USA: Intermagnetics MRI system cleared by FDA.
newsitem.headline: Intermagnetics MRI system cleared by FDA.

text.p: Intermagnetics General Corp said Tuesday that its new magnetic resonance imaging system had been reviewed and may now be marketed in the United States.

The company said that IMiG-MRI L.L.C, its joint venture with Surrey Medical Imaging Systems Ltd of England, was officially notified by the Food and Drug Administration that the "premarket notification" that the IMiG-MRI system may be marketed in the U.S. to the medical diagnostic industry, subject to the general controls provisions of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act .
Premarket notification, submitted last year to the FDA, is required for new medical equipment by section 510(k) of the FDC Act.

The information required in such a submission includes: technical performance and safety data; product description and specifications; procedures for software development and testing; example output; and promotional literature. MRI systems are defined by federal statute as "class II" medical devices, which means that an MRI 510(k) notification may be based on the assertion that the system is substantially equivalent to a predicate device: i.e., class I or class II devices legally marketed by other companies.

The FDA finding that the IMiG-MRI system is substantially equivalent to predicate devices allows the marketing of the product in the United States. The FDA prohibits companies from stating that the substantially equivalent finding constitutes "official approval."

The system is designed to provide high-quality diagnostic images at the lowest possible cost. Notable technical features of the system include: an oval-shaped patient opening which is larger than either conventional superconducting magnets or so-called "open" permanent magnets; a metal-free permanent magnet design which both eliminates many technical imaging problems and avoids the necessity to replace cryogens; and a PC-based computer architecture which is cost-effective, easy to operate, and easy to upgrade.
